entry.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
entry.summary: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.

entry.title: A sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines
entry.summary: We construct a sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines in the real projective plane. It is obtained from the icosahedral arrangement $\mathcal{A}(21,2)$ by adjoining the $30$ images of the line $y+\sqrt{\varphi}\,z=0$ under the rotation group of the icosahedron, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. Its intersection multiplicities are $t_2=120$, $t_3=190$, $t_5=36$, and $t_6=15$, with all other $t_r$ zero. These counts give equality in Melchior's inequality and hence prove simpliciality. The arrangement is irreducible, belongs to neither of the two known infinite families of irreducible simplicial arrangements, and is not supersolvable. It therefore disproves the $37$-line bound for sporadic arrangements conjectured by Cuntz and Mücksch. We give explicit coordinates, a finite incidence certificate, a geometric explanation of the parameter $\sqrt{\varphi}$, and a standalone exact-arithmetic verifier.

entry.title: A Hyperplane Bound and Ward's Divisibility Conjecture
entry.summary: Let $q=p^f$, where $p$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-ary linear code meeting the Griesmer bound, with positive dimension and minimum distance $d\ge1$, is $p^{\max\{0,ν_p(d)-f+1\}}$-divisible, as asserted in Ward's conjecture. Arbitrary projective column multiplicities are allowed. The geometric ingredient is a bound independent of dimension: a nonzero scalar-invariant function $F:\mathbb{F}_q^k\to\mathbb{F}_p$, with $F(0)=0$ and prime-field algebraic degree at most $(f+s)(p-1)$, vanishes identically on at most $p^s(q-1)$ linear hyperplanes when $0\le s<f$. A truncated digit-sum inequality forces selected coefficient polynomials to be homogeneous of ordinary degree less than $q$. Weighted moments on a projective line then bound their linear factors, while a second-moment argument handles the complementary support configuration. An elementary finite-difference calculation supplies the degree bound for divided weight residues. Endpoint shortenings prove the basic divisibility layers; endpoint lifting, a surjective linear functional, and residual-code induction extend the argument to every valuation. We include the proofs of the classical ingredients, identify their sources, and distinguish the present argument from an earlier reported unpublished proof.

entry.title: GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields
entry.summary: We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin. The second is a special case of the (geometric) abc conjecture proposed by Vojta, which compares the truncated counting function and the usual counting function. This is a compact analogue of a theorem of Guo, Nguyen, Sun and Wang, and also resolves a conjecture of Buium, which was only known for traceless abelian varieties or constant abelian varieties previously. The proofs of these inequalities follow a common three-step pattern: from microscopic local estimates to local estimates, and then to global estimates. Building on the canonical Xie-Yuan heights, we control discrete counting functions by continuous integrals of Betti forms. The main new tools are uniform Nevanlinna-type estimates for families of linear entire curves on abelian varieties; combined with covering arguments based on Besicovitch theory and averaging, these handle overlaps and gaps precisely.

entry.title: New Qualitative and Quantitative Estimates for Neumann Eigenvalues toward Pólya's Conjecture
entry.summary: We introduce the Enhanced Neumann Pólya inequality, which is stronger than Pólya's conjecture, and verify it for many classes of domains, including strip-tiling domains, Euclidean balls, thin product domains, and certain higher-dimensional tiling domains. We develop a geometric removal approach for the Enhanced Neumann Pólya inequality. In particular, our results provide new classes of domains satisfying the Neumann part of Pólya's conjecture.

entry.title: The $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures-Wasserstein barycenters)
entry.summary: We study the $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures-Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fréchet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.
entry.arxiv:comment: 20 pages; 4 appendices; one synthetic experiment included

entry.title: From Cauchy to Gaussian: Sharp Lower Deviations and Ehrhard-Type Inequality
entry.summary: We establish dimension-free, pointwise optimal lower-deviation bounds for convex functions under spherically symmetric Cauchy-type measures. These bounds use either mean-variance normalization or moments about the median, the latter covering the Cauchy case where the mean and variance are unavailable. By approximation with a parametrized family the Cauchy-type measures, our results recover the Gaussian setting of Paouris and Valettas \cite{PaourisValettas18} and strengthen their variance-sensitive estimate to a sharp bound, with a complete equality characterization. This goes beyond the partial improvements obtained in subsequent work. We also prove an Ehrhard-type inequality for arbitrary convex sets under these Cauchy-type measures in every dimension and characterize all equality cases. This resolves a conjecture posed by Byczkowski, Małecki and Żak \cite{ByczkowskiMaleckiZak22}. The proof follows from a variational argument combined with the joint concavity of fiber rearrangement. The geometric inequality reduces distributions of convex observables to one-dimensional convex transforms, yielding the sharp lower-deviation bounds.

entry.title: Lie weights for CM curves and unipotent Selmer dimensions
entry.summary: We prove an equidistribution result for Galois characters in the graded Lie components $L_n$ associated to the $\mathbf{Q}_p$-fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve $X$ over a number field $k$ with geometrically CM Jacobian. That is, we consider the $p$-adic completion of a fixed character lattice, where we define measures $μ_n$ counting normalized character multiplicities in $L_n$, and show that $(μ_n)_n$ weakly converges to the Haar measure. The key idea to prove convergence is to write the Fourier coefficients of $μ_n$ in terms of traces of operators on $L_n$ induced by symplectic operators on the Tate module, and control them with a known symplectic character formula, followed by Weyl's criterion for compact abelian groups. Our main arithmetic application is to combine equidistribution with the Iwasawa-theoretic method of Coates--Kim and a compactness argument for moving analytic loci, giving a dimension inequality for unipotent Selmer schemes: $\dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}H^1_f(G_{k,T},U_n)< \dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}\prod_{v\mid p}H^1_f(G_v,U_n)$ for all sufficiently large $n,$ with the quotient having limit superior at most $1/2.$ This answers a particular case of a conjecture by Kim, from which the finiteness of $X(\mathbf{Q})$ can be recovered when $k=\mathbf{Q}.$

entry.title: Sharp detection thresholds for random geometric graphs with polynomial average degrees
entry.summary: We study the random geometric graph formed by connecting $n$ independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ whenever their inner product exceeds a threshold chosen to give edge density $p$. We establish the conjectured dimensionality threshold for indistinguishability from the Erdös-Rényi graph $G(n,p)$ throughout the sparse regime with polynomially growing average degree. Specifically, for every fixed $δ>0$, if $p\to0$, $p\ge n^{-1+δ}$, and $d\gg (np\log(1/p))^3$, then the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the two distributions vanishes. Our proof builds on the posterior analysis framework introduced in previous work of the authors, combining a truncated second moment analysis with Fourier and spherical harmonic expansions. As in prior works, we reduce the KL bound to controlling a truncated $χ^2$-divergence $Δ$ for the neighborhood of the last vertex conditional on the graph induced by the preceding vertices. We then bound $Δ$ using a Fourier expansion of the conditional likelihood ratio for this neighborhood, where the high-frequency contribution is made negligible by truncation to a typical-degree event, while a spherical harmonic expansion approximates the low-frequency contribution in terms of posterior moments of bounded-degree harmonic polynomials. The key observation is that these moments and $Δ$ satisfy a coupled system of cavity recurrences, yielding a self-bounding inequality that implies the desired KL bound.

entry.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincaré Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
entry.summary: The Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincaré constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. We give a deterministic variational proof with an explicit bound on the Poincaré constant $C_P(μ)\le25$, where $μ$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. Starting from elliptic moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on normalized Appell coefficient norms through \emph{joint} maximization over the measure and test function. Variation of the measure gives a maximum-principle inequality, while stationarity in the test function controls the highest-order cumulant terms. Two concave barriers constructed from quadratic and cubic polynomials close the induction. A weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition then controls the curl correction of weighted divergence, yielding a curvature estimate for compatible symmetric tensor fields that is uniform in rank. Quadratic duality converts this estimate into an operator comparison for centered integration, linking the coefficient bounds to control of the inverse gradient. A spectral-radius estimate and a scalar growth inequality for adjoint iterates then yield the Poincaré bound. The final estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to complete the proof for general isotropic log-concave measures.
